Tonight's team to face Crystal Palace! ​​💪🩵XI | Donnarumma, Khusanov, Dias (C), Gvardiol, O'Reilly, Anderson, Guéhi, Foden, Cherki, Semenyo, HaalandSUBS | Rulli, Kovačić, Aït-Nouri, Reis, Echeverri, Bouaddi, McAidoo, Braithwaite, Lewis🤝 @etihad pic.twitter.com/qNgJPXKDM7

The second weekend of the Premier League season kicks off under the lights in South London as Crystal Palace host Manchester City at Selhurst Park. Manchester City won both fixtures 3-0 last season and they are in fact unbeaten in their last 11 Premier league away games against Crystal Palace, who have won just two of the 22 top flight meetings.

Crystal Palace experienced defeat on the opening weekend, falling to a 2-0 loss at Everton last Saturday, meaning the Pierre Sage era started with a defeat. Tonight is Sage’s first home game in charge of the club.

“I think it will be a wonderful moment, but I prefer to have a wonderful moment with good news at the end of the game,” Sage said. “That is why I do not think about me in this situation. The most important thing is the team and the result for sure, because we prepare all the week for that, to make them [the fans] happy. They will be happy to see us, but I think they would prefer to see us win. I will give my life to make them happy. I cannot do more. When you are in this stadium [Selhurst Park], you feel the history. You feel that there is something heavy weighing on you. It is a great responsibility that I have been entrusted with. We cannot wait to see this stadium in action.”

Sage has confirmed that Ismaila Sarr, who has been linked with a move away from the club this summer, and Chadi Riad will miss out tonight due to injury, as will striker Jean-Philippe Mateta. Palace have confirmed the addition of Axel Disasi on loan from Chelsea and the French defender could be involved tonight.

Manchester City appeared to be heading towards defeat in Enzo Maresca’s first league game in charge of the club last weekend. They were 1-0 down at home against Bournemouth in the closing stages before goals from Marc Guehi and Josko Gvardiol gave them a come-from-behind win.

It has been a busy week in the transfer window for Manchester City. Both Savio (formerly Savinho) and Omar Marmoush have left for Tottenham, joining a long list of departures from the Etihad this summer. Moroccan midfielder Ayyoub Bouaddi has arrived in an £85m deal from Lille and has become the most expensive teenager in Premier League history. Maresca has confirmed that 18-year-old Bouaddi is ready to start.

“He [Bouaddi] is ready,” Maresca said. “He was working with his former club so he is fit. We will see how long he needs in terms of adaptation but he is ready to go. He is quite calm. He does not look 18, he already looks older, which is important. But in this case, we need to go slowly because he is very young, he has come from a different country so there is no rush for him. He is going to help us now and in the future. He is very mature for being 18.”

Team news from Selhurst Park to follow shortly.

#1774. Man United XI vs Sporting: Starting lineup, confirmed team news, injury latest for Champions League today

The Standard's journalism is supported by our readers. If you click links to other sites on this page, we will earn commission.

Luke Shaw is only fit enough for the bench as Manchester United face Sporting this evening.

The left-back has missed the last eight games across all competitions with a muscular injury, but could make his return in Lisbon.

New head coach Mauricio Pochettino endured a horror start to his Man Utd tenure with a heavy 4-0 defeat by rivals Liverpool in the Premier League on Sunday.

The Red Devils were down to 10 men after just eight minutes at Anfield when Leny Yoro fouled Alexander Isak and received a red card, which has since been overturned following a successful appeal.

United suffered no new injury blows on Merseyside, but the result was “painful” according to Pochettino, and he will be looking to put things right immediately in Europe’s top competition on Wednesday night.

The former Tottenham and Chelsea boss sprung a surprise with the inclusion of Matthijs de Ligt in his starting XI against Liverpool, with the Dutchman having previously been sidelined for a year with a persistent back injury.

The centre-back looked awkward for much of the match, and his selection was scrutinised intensely afterwards.

And he unsurprisingly does not keep his place in Lisbon, with Harry Maguire restored.

That could see Lisandro Martinez plugged in at left-back once more if Shaw is not ready to start, although the Argentine had to shift inside after Yoro’s red card against Liverpool, with Patrick Dorgu then moving back.

Diogo Dalot failed to impress on Sunday and sees himself rotated out for Noussair Mazraoui, while in the engine room, Youri Tielemans was hooked for Mason Mount in the second half. The Belgian keeps his place.

Bryan Mbeumo was the man sacrificed following the early sending off at Liverpool as Pochettino resorted to damage limitation, but the Cameroon international should make a quick return here.

Matheus Cunha led the attack but was replaced by Joshua Zirkzee at half-time. The Brazilian is suspended tonight, however.

On the injury list remain Benjamin Sesko, Marcus Rashford, Carlos Baleba and Manuel Ugarte, while back-up goalkeeper Karl Darlow has also yet to return.

Confirmed Man Utd XI vs Sporting (4-2-3-1): Lammens; Yoro, Maguire, Martinez, Mazraoui; Tielemans, Mainoo; Amad, Fernandes, Mbeumo; Zirkzee

#1773. Serie A preview: AC Milan vs. Frosinone – Team news, opposition insight, stats and prediction

Milan will return to action on Sunday evening, hoping to pick up where they left off before the international break with a strong performance against Frosinone.

If we look at the league, it has been a very decent start to the season for Ruben Amorim and his men. However, they are yet to win three games on the trot, so tomorrow’s encounter is a fantastic chance for them to really show their worth.

Read SempreMilan ad-free and get access to exclusive news. Click here for a free trial!

It won’t be easy, though. Amorim said during his press conference that it’s hard to identify the movement patterns of Frosinone, who certainly have the ability to make life difficult for the Rossoneri.

Game date: Sunday, November 22 Kick-off time: 18:00 (CET) Venue: San Siro Referee: Luca Pairetto (VAR: Pezzuto)

Some good news arrived on Saturday morning as Strahinja Pavlovic was deemed fit enough to be called up for the game. It’s not certain whether he will start or not, but Amorim at least said that he’s happy to have the Serbian and ‘his fire’ back.

A few days ago, it was also confirmed that Mike Maignan will be at the manager’s disposal despite the injury scare with France. Of course, it’s not all perfect on the injury front as Matteo Gabbia, Fikayo Tomori, Ruben Loftus-Cheek, Alexis Saelemaekers and Samuel Chukwueze are still sidelined.

Anyway, moving on to the predicted starting eleven, it was initially thought that Amorim would field the same one as we saw against Genoa. However, he made it very clear during the presser that Musah won’t play as a left-back, so there will indeed be some changes.

According to the latest reports, the American will still start but in midfield instead, allowing Adrien Rabiot to have a slightly more advanced role. It also means that Davide Bartesaghi will come into the eleven, currently ahead of Pervis Estupinan in the race.

Alphadjo Cisse has been in red-hot form lately but it seems Amorim wants to manage expectations a little, with the youngster tipped to start on the bench. Christian Pulisic should thus have a role on the flank as opposed to in the centre, although one would imagine everything will be a bit fluid.

It’s no surprise to see that Goncalo Ramos should start up front, but of course, he will need to get going with the goalscoring sooner rather than later. Francesco Camarda is knocking on the door, as is Cisse who has been tested in that role before.

Predicted Milan XI (4-3-3): Maignan; Gila, De Winter, Diawara, Bartesaghi; Musah, Modric, Rabiot; Moreira, Ramos, Pulisic.

Predicted bench: Torriani, P. Terracciano, F. Terracciano, Pavlovic, Vladimirov, Estupinan, Jashari, Comotto, Hutchinson, Cisse, Camarda.

Injuries & suspensions: Gabbia, Tomori, Loftus-Cheek, Saelemaekers and Chukwueze.

Frosinone have definitely been one of the surprises of the season so far. After a very strong Serie B campaign with 81 points and only three games lost, they secured direct promotion to the top tier (finishing second) and have been making the most of the adventure.

They are currently on 20 points after eleven games, winning six, drawing two and losing three, which has put them in sixth place. That’s very strong for a newcomer and for a coach who is only in his second season with the club, especially considering the upset against Como.

It’s the 56-year-old’s second attempt at Serie A after coaching Cremonese for half a season in 2022-23. He didn’t manage a single win then, so you can definitely say that the performance so far has been great revenge for him.

So, what is behind this rise? As pointed out by Gazzetta dello Sport, the direct style of play has been key for Frosinone. As opposed to Milan, who want to see a lot of the ball, they are willing to have less possession and break on the counter.

It doesn’t mean that they sit back, though. In fact, it has been the opposite as they are the highest-pressing team in the league. The strategy thus seems to be to force mistakes out of the opponents, while also making sure that they are direct in possession.

While collective effort deserves most of the praise, it has definitely helped that the likes of Giacomo Calo, Giorgi Kvernadze and Antonio Raimondo – among others – have performed at a very high level. They aren’t exactly big-name players, so a lot of them are having their breakout seasons.

Moving on to actual team news, the situation up front is not ideal for Frosinone as their top scorer, the aforementioned Antonio Raimondo, is out injured. Birigilea, who is on two goals, is set to replace him in the No.9 position.

The Milan academy product Sebastiano Desplanches, who left the club four years ago, will be on the bench. He’s yet to make an appearance this season, with Alvini preferring Lorenzo Palmisani instead.

Predicted Frosinone XI (4-2-3-1): Palmisani; Oyono, Calvani, Monterisi, Terzic; Calo, Masini; Ghedjemis; Schmid, Kvernadze; Birigilea.

Predicted bench: Desplanches, Pisseri, Cittadini, Tchato, Amey, Akpoguma, Fayed, El Azzouzi, Cichella, Hasa, Fini, Zerbin, Bobcek.

Injuries & suspensions: Bracaglia, Grillitsch and Raimondo.

This fixture has only been played six times, but even with such a small sample size, it’s clear that Milan are the favourites with four wins and two draws so far. They have won the last three as well, spread across the 2023-24 and 2018-19 seasons.

That said, the most recent encounter was a dramatic one, if you like. Olivier Giroud opened the scoring for Milan away from home but then Frosinone scored twice. Thanks to goals from Matteo Gabbia and Luka Jovic, the Rossoneri were able to turn it back in their favour.

The last time at San Siro, meanwhile, it was a great 3-1 win as Jovic, Pulisic and Tomori found the back of the net. Most of you will remember the American’s goal, as it was Maignan who assisted him with a fantastic pass.

➤ Milan are unbeaten in all six previous meetings against Frosinone in Serie A (W4 D2): among the teams against which they have never lost in the competition, the Rossoneri have played more games only against Pisa (14 – six also against Crotone and Lecco).

➤ Milan have scored at least three goals in four of their six Serie A matches against Frosinone, producing 15 goals overall, an average of 2.5 per game. Only against Pescara (2.9) have they recorded a higher average, among the opponents they have faced on at least five occasions (2.5 also against Casale and Messina).

➤ Frosinone have won six games this season, drawing two and losing three. Only three newly promoted teams in the last 40 years have recorded more wins in their first 12 Serie A games of the season: Bari in 1994/95 (seven), Chievo in 2001/02 (seven), and Hellas Verona in 2013/14 (seven).

➤ Milan have won four of their last five league games (L1), scoring at least two goals in each, after failing to win three of their previous four (D3). The last time they scored more than one goal in consecutive Serie A matches was between September 2020 and January 2021, when they managed 15 games.

➤ Although Frosinone are unbeaten in three of their five away games this season (W1 D2), they have won just two of their last 27 away games in Serie A (including previous participations), with 10 draws and 15 defeats.

➤ Milan have failed to win four of their last seven Serie A games played after the international break (D2 L2). On the other hand, Frosinone are unbeaten in three of their last five top-flight matches immediately following Italy matches (W2 D1).

➤ Frosinone have attempted the most counterattacks from advantageous situations in Serie A this season: 22, almost double the number of any other team. On the other hand, Milan are the only team that haven’t allowed a single counterattack when trailing in the current campaign.

➤ Only Juventus (79) have attempted more long-range shots than Frosinone (77) this season. On the other hand, Milan are the team that have attempted the fewest shots from outside the area (30) and the one that have conceded the most shots from outside the area in relation to the total conceded, 44%.

➤ Adrien Rabiot has earned the most points for his team from direct goal contributions this season, having scored 10 goals and assisted four times. In the most recent matchday, he became the first Milan midfielder to be involved in at least one goal in six consecutive league appearances since Kaká in 2004 (who managed seven).

➤ Only Matías Soulé (80) has been involved in more sequences ending with a shot than Giacomo Calò (76) in this Serie A. The Frosinone player has scored five goals in the current campaign and only one midfielder has scored more goals in the first 12 matchdays in the top flight for a newly promoted team in the three points for a win era: Hidetoshi Nakata with Perugia in 1998/99 (six).

Since Frosinone like to play on the counterattacks, one player who I think could be crucial for Milan is Musah. As he’s set to start in midfield and not at left-back, the feeling is that his main role will be to prevent the opponents from having too much open space on the counter.

Further up the pitch, I’m excited to see Moreira. He got himself a goal in Belgium’s win over Italy and he has looked a lot better on the right flank ever since the derby performance. He can definitely make the difference with his skill.

As for Frosinone, it’s obvious that Calo is the man whom Milan will want to stop. He likes to dictate the play and if he’s allowed too much time on the ball, identifying his teammates in good positions, then there could be trouble for the Rossoneri.

It will also be interesting to see if Birigilea can fill the shoes of Raimondo. He bagged a brace against Lecce but in the last two games, he failed to find the back of the net. He will surely be keen to get back on target.

A lot of people are expecting this to be a high-scoring affair and that’s a very reasonable take, given how both teams play. That said, I think this could be one where Milan actually get their defence in order and don’t concede, even if that might be a somewhat optimistic prediction.

#1772. Liverpool XI vs Club Brugge: Starting lineup, confirmed team news, injury latest for Champions League today

The Standard's journalism is supported by our readers. If you click links to other sites on this page, we will earn commission.

Liverpool are without Cody Gakpo and Ryan Gravenberch for their Champions League clash with Club Brugge tonight.

The Dutch duo were both absent for Sunday’s 4-0 thrashing of fierce rivals Manchester United in the Premier League and won’t return as Andoni Iraola’s side head to Belgium on Wednesday.

"I think with Cody it's a soleus injury, it's a muscle injury,” Iraola said at his pre-match press conference. "It's not a big thing but I think we expected that he was out. He's going to be out even for the weekend [against Everton]. It's more predictable.

"With Ryan, it's difficult to say. I think he is having pain. These things in the fascia are difficult to solve.

"You know sometimes it's about managing the pain, but now it's not in a good place and let's see if we can find ways to solve a little bit the problem. But injuries [like this] are not easy to go normally."

In Gravenberch’s absence, Trey Nyoni gets the nod in midfield alongside Florian Wirtz.

Jeremie Frimpong and Virgil van Dijk were welcome returnees against United following respective injury scares, while Rio Ngumoha played a starring role in the demolition job on Sunday in place of Gakpo on the left flank. The phenomenal young winger gets a rest here, though, as do his club captain and Alexis Mac Allister.

Alexander Isak led the line by example on Sunday, and gets the nod once more here, with Hugo Ekitike still recovering from his Achilles rupture.

Neither Giovanni Leoni nor Conor Bradley are fit enough to make the squad, though they are thought to be closing in on returns from their respective long-term knee injuries.

Confirmed Liverpool XI vs Club Brugge (4-2-3-1): Alisson; Frimpong, Araujo, Jacquet, Kerkez, Nyoni, Szoboszlai, Wirtz, Isak, Munoz, Barcola

Subs: Mamardashvili, Woodman, Gomez, Van Dijk, Mac Allister, Tsimikas, Chambers, McConnell, Koumas, Ngumoha, Danns

Injured: Ekitike, Gakpo, Gravenberch, Bradley, Leoni

Time and date: 8pm GMT on Wednesday November 25, 2026

#1771. The Preview: It's time for Hibs boss Reedijk to bring sunshine back to Leith

Published: 16:03 EST, 20 November 2026 | Updated: 16:18 EST, 20 November 2026

Hibernian supporters know all too well the dangers associated with getting one’s hopes up.

It’s a road they’ve been down time and time again, only to end up with that same familiar sickening feeling in the pit of their stomach at the end of it.

Which is why any talk of the Edinburgh club experiencing some sort of mini-revival should quite rightly be taken with more than a large pinch of salt.

Let’s not forget, at the start of the month, new boss Marink Reedijk had picked up a paltry point from his four games in charge since taking the reins from David Gray.

A statement win over Hearts at Hampden to book their Premier Sports Cup final spot was backed up with an emphatic 4-0 dismantling of Aberdeen up at Pittodrie.

Hibs manager Marink Reedijk is still searching for his first victory at Easter Road

Credit where it’s due, of course. Both victories were hard-earned and thoroughly deserved.

But it’s important not to read too much in to either of them. Players going above and beyond in a derby clash should be a given, while the Dons appeared to have chucked it altogether under the stewardship of former manager Stephen Robinson long before Hibs turned up in the Granite City.

The real test begins this weekend with the visit of Dundee United, as Reedijk’s men look to secure a first home Premiership win in over seven months.

The fans have been crying out for entertainment in Leith for far longer than that. In the latter days of Gray’s reign, the atmosphere at Easter Road was verging on toxic.

Reedijk needs to change that, and now has two games against the Dundee clubs over the next four days to get the momentum swinging in the opposite direction.

Continuing to get the best out of his midfield three will be key to that.

The reintroduction of Joe Newell to the starting XI has paid off big-time. Not so much in terms of the stats, but rather what he allows Miguel Chaiwa and Josh Mulligan to do.

The former was linked with a move to Celtic over the summer, but looked miles off it in the early weeks of the campaign until Newell lined up alongside him.

Chaiwa can be guilty of trying to carry out too many jobs in the middle of the park, but Newell’s calming influence has enabled him to stick to what he’s good at — namely breaking up the play and moving the ball on to his more creative team-mates in front of him.

There’s no doubt the Zambian is at his best when he keeps things simple.

Joe Newell has provided a calming influence in the middle of the park amid this upturn in form

Newell’s presence has also freed Mulligan to play further up the field rather than on the fringes of his own box, where he was popping up far too often a couple of months ago. He’s wasted back there.

If he can add some more goals and assists to his name over the next few, there is every chance he can play himself in to the thoughts of Scotland boss Sebastien Pocognoli ahead of the next set of internationals.

It should be an intriguing battle this afternoon in the engine room, with United boasting the most cohesive midfield group in the top flight with Dylan Tait, Lyall Cameron and Zidane Iqbal.

Of course, even if Hibs deliver in that sense, it may count for very little if the guys at the top end of the pitch can’t do the business. The lack of cutting edge has been an ongoing concern. Four goals against Aberdeen doesn't change that.

Owen Elding appears to be Reedijk’s preferred option in the central striker role, but while the young Irishman has shown flashes of his potential, he has offered little to suggest he can be relied upon to find the net on a consistent basis.

The problem is, can anyone? Record-signing Thibault Klidje may have opened his league account for the season against the Dons, however we’ve seen enough to know that he isn’t the answer.

Ante Suto is in the same boat, while Stoke City loanee Nathan Lowe has struggled for both game time and form.

And as for Rabbi Matondo? Well, the wait goes on to see any real return on that investment. Early days, mind you.

That Martin Boyle remains Hibs’ main goalscoring threat is troubling, especially given that the veteran can’t even be considered a nailed-on starter these days.

There are a significant number of players — across all areas of the park — fighting for their future at the club. Indeed, you would imagine Reedijk is counting down the days until January when he will look to freshen up the squad with guys more suited to his style.

Lyall Cameron has been a key man behind Dundee United's surge up the Premiership table

Hibs should use today’s opponents as an example of how patience can pay off.

It’s fair to say that Jim Goodwin has never been Mr. Popular in and around Tannadice. Goodness knows why.

Many fans were calling for his head as recently as the summer after failing to secure a top-six finish last term, but he is slowly but surely starting to win over his doubters.

Make no mistake, this season presents a golden opportunity for United to seriously challenge for third spot.

You never know what you’re going to get from Hearts on any given week, while this is very much uncharted territory for Falkirk.

And let’s face it, nobody would expect the likes of Hibs, Aberdeen or Motherwell to claw themselves into contention.

While everyone else tries to stumble their way through a period of transition, United’s consistency – both on and off the park – could prove to be the difference.

#1770. Is Matheus Cunha injured? Why Manchester United star isn’t in squad to face Sporting

Mauricio Pochettino will not be able to call on Matheus Cunha as he chases his first win with Manchester United.

The Red Devils’ new boss is facing just his second match in charge of the club as he looks to bounce back from the weekend’s chastening 4-0 defeat by Liverpool.

He will return to the Champions League for the first time since leaving Paris Saint-Germain this evening, with a tricky tie away at Sporting on the docket.

However, in a selection blow, he will not be able to make use of one of his more threatening forwards, with Cunha left out of the Lisbon-bound travelling squad.

There was some positive news in the squad, though, as Luke Shaw and Karl Darlow came back into contention after injury layoffs, but the absence of Cunha is a serious setback for Pochettino as he looks to breathe life into his nascent United tenure.

Matheus Cunha was left out of the travelling squad for Manchester United’s meeting with Sporting as he is serving a red card suspension.

The Brazilian forward was dismissed in second-half injury time as United came from behind to beat Roma 3-2 last time out in the Champions League.

Having trailed by two goals to nil with just 17 minutes played, a second-half penalty from Bruno Fernandes and a quickfire brace from Cunha flipped the script.

Cunha, though, was shown two yellow cards in a chaotic finish.

The first came when he removed his shirt celebrating what proved to be the winning goal, and he picked up a second in the 91st minute for a needless, reckless late tackle on Leonardo Balerdi.

He will serve his suspension against Sporting tonight and be available again when United host RB Leipzig in two weeks’ time, on December 8.

#1769. Mauricio Pochettino explains surprise Manchester United squad decision for Sporting clash: ‘Great opportunity’

Mauricio Pochettino has explained his decision to hand Joshua Zirkzee a first start of the season against Sporting in the Champions League.

The Argentine named just his second United team in Lisbon on Wednesday evening as he looked to bounce back from a damning 4-0 defeat by Liverpool on his managerial bow.

In Portugal, he made four changes from the side he named at Anfield, with Harry Maguire, Noussair Mazraoui and Amad Diallo all coming into the side.

Perhaps his most notable call, though, saw striker Zirkzee chosen to lead the line, making his first start of the campaign.

The Dutchman has been bumped up the pecking order somewhat for this match, with fellow striker Benjamin Sesko out injured and deputy Matheus Cunha suspended.

Pochettino, though, said he hopes Zirkzee can kick on as a more dependable option, given United’s thin ranks.

Asked to explain the selection, he told TNT Sports: “Cunha is suspended, of course, Sesko is injured. I think it is a great opportunity for Josh (Zirkzee) to show his quality.

“I think it is an important game to start to think that he can be a very important player for the team, and today is an opportunity for him.”

Zirkzee was entirely peripheral under Michael Carrick and had looked to leave United in the summer transfer window. He was the subject of a loan bid from Everton on Deadline Day, but no move materialised.

Pochettino, though, seems optimistic he can bring Zirkzee in from the cold as United look to salvage their campaign, both domestically and abroad.

#1768. Club Brugge vs. Liverpool: How to watch, date, time, live stream, TV channel

By Saikat Mandal | 24 Nov 2026 10:52

Liverpool will be looking to make it three consecutive victories across all competitions when they travel to Belgium to take on Club Brugge at the Jan Breydel Stadium in the Champions League on Wednesday.

Both sides have collected nine points from their opening four matches, with the Reds holding a slender advantage over their Belgian counterparts courtesy of a marginally superior goal scored.

Liverpool have already overcome Spanish opposition in the shape of Atletico Madrid and Villarreal, while also registering an emphatic 6-3 victory over LASK Linz, although their campaign suffered a setback with a 3-2 defeat to Fenerbahce in their most recent European outing.

Club Brugge, meanwhile, began their Champions League campaign with a 3-2 home defeat to Aston Villa but responded impressively, reeling off three successive victories against Inter Milan, Lens and PSV Eindhoven.

Here, Sports Mole provides everything you need to know about how to tune into the contest.

Club Brugge vs Liverpool is one of nine fixtures scheduled for matchday five of the Champions League, with several of Europe's leading clubs, including Barcelona and Paris Saint-Germain taking to the pitch on Wednesday.

The eagerly anticipated contest at the Jan Breydel Stadium is among the seven matches scheduled to kick off at 8pm UK time, while the remaining two fixtures will get underway earlier, at 5.45pm.

The match will take place at the Jan Breydel Stadium in Bruges, Belgium, which serves as the home ground of two top-flight rivals, Club Brugge and Cercle Brugge.

The multi-purpose venue has a seating capacity of 29,042 and takes its name from Jan Breydel, an instigator of the Bruges Matins, the uprising that culminated in the 1302 Battle of the Golden Spurs.

The match will be available to watch live in the UK on TNT Sports 2 and HBO Max. International viewers can tune in via Paramount+ in the United States, Sony Ten in India and Stan Sport in Australia.

The match will be available to stream on HBO Max in the UK, Paramount+, DAZN and Amazon Prime Video in the United States, SonyLIV in India, and Stan Sport in Australia.

The official X accounts of Club Brugge and Liverpool are expected to share match clips and updates throughout the contest, while journalists covering the fixture may also post their own footage and updates.

Following the final whistle, extended highlights should be available on both clubs' official YouTube channels, with viewers in the UK also able to catch the action again on TNT Sports.

Club Brugge are in excellent form at present, having gone unbeaten in their last 11 matches across all competitions, winning 10 of them.

Ivan Leko's side are also brimming with confidence after recording three consecutive victories in the Champions League, and another win against Liverpool would put them in a strong position to secure automatic qualification for the knockout stages.

Liverpool, meanwhile, head into this fixture on the back of a morale-boosting 4-0 victory over arch-rivals Manchester United at Anfield, and Andoni Iraola will be determined to keep that momentum going.

Rio Ngumoha produced a dazzling display against the Red Devils and could retain his place in the absence of Cody Gakpo, while Trey Nyoni, who scored against Fenerbahce, could also come into the midfield.

A victory away from home in the Champions League would provide the squad with a significant lift ahead of their Merseyside derby later this week.

#1766. Alexander Isak closes in on Mohamed Salah record with latest Liverpool goal

Alexander Isak is closing in on a record held by Mohamed Salah with his latest Liverpool goal.

The Swedish striker did not take long to open the scoring as Liverpool faced Club Brugge in the Champions League on Wednesday night.

Bradley Barcola won the ball high up the pitch to set the Reds on the attack and Dominik Szoboszlai teed Isak up to finish from close range.

It was a significant goal for Isak, who has now scored in six consecutive away matches for Liverpool.

It is a feat that very few men have bettered. According to the stat gurus at Opta, no Liverpool player has ever scored in more than seven consecutive away appearances.

Salah is the current record holder, and should Isak find the back of the net in this weekend’s Merseyside derby at the Hill Dickinson Stadium, he would equal the Egyptian king’s record. Add another against Chelsea at Stamford Bridge on December 5, and he could surpass it.

Prior to the launch of the Premier League, Sam English, John Evans and John Aldridge all scored in seven consecutive away matches.

Salah called time on his Liverpool career at the end of last season, leaving with 257 goals and 123 assists across 442 appearances.

He now plies his trade in Turkey with Trabzonspor, where he has made a bright start to life, tallying 16 goal contributions in his first 17 appearances.

By Axel Clody | 24 Nov 2026 11:18

With Fermin Lopez having attracted the attention of several Premier League heavyweights, ready to invest large sums, Barcelona have taken a stance on the future of their attacking midfielder.

Fermin Lopez has stepped up under Hansi Flick. The Spanish attacking midfielder is increasingly establishing himself as a starter. His statistics since the start of the season prove it: 16 games played, 12 of them as a starter, with nine goals and seven assists. His performances and talent have drawn attention in the market.

Fermin Lopez nevertheless extended his contract until June 2031 at the start of the year and has a release clause of £425m (€500m). This move would allow the club to reward the player's progress and strengthen his place in the squad.

#1764. Liverpool hit with concerning injury blow as star forced off early in Champions League clash

Liverpool have been hit with a major injury blow as Victor Munoz was forced off in the first half of their Champions League meeting with Club Brugge.

The young Spaniard threw himself into an aggressive challenge on Jorne Spileers shortly before half-time - but came off far worse after appearing to knock knees with the Belgian.

Munoz looked to be in considerable pain as he stayed down and Liverpool’s medical staff were waved onto the pitch. There was a lengthy delay as he received treatment.

He was surrounded by concerned-looking team-mates as a stretcher was brought on to carry him off, but it was waved away and Munoz was able to leave the pitch under his own steam.

The fact he was able to do so suggests his injury may not be too severe, though Munoz still appeared to be in serious discomfort as he made his way to the bench with a pronounced limp.

Rio Ngumoha was brought on in his place, and Andoni Iraola will issue an update on his condition at full-time.

Liverpool were one to the good when Munoz left the pitch, after Dominik Szoboszlai teed Alexander Isak up to score from the edge of the six-yard box with 13 minutes on the clock.

#1763. Mauricio Pochettino must fix a club stuck in a constant cycle of failure. The new Man United boss has the personality but the squad is a mish-mash and where he sits as a coach is a great unknown, writes IAN LADYMAN

Published: 16:51 EST, 20 November 2026 | Updated: 17:07 EST, 20 November 2026

In a soft-focus Sky TV interview that followed Mauricio Pochettino’s opening press conference on Friday, the Manchester United chief executive Omar Berrada revealed there had been a ‘buzz’ about the club since the arrival of their new manager.

Whether he was speaking metaphorically or referring to the sound of drones stealing Pochettino’s training secrets from above only he will know.

As is usually the case these days, much about the modern United remains unclear.

But what we do know after welcoming the eighth full-time manager since the days of Sir Alex Ferguson is that once again England’s biggest football club is relying on a personality lift to drag them back to their feet.

This is what happens when you get things wrong for so long, when you buy the wrong players and install executives who appear to be learning on the job. You end up hiring and firing managers, waiting for the one who finally arrives with the magic dust, the capacity to somehow create something greater than the sum of the rather wonky parts.

Listening to Pochettino here – a talented coach and a good person – was to occasionally think back to words spoken in the weeks of their arrivals on this territory by predecessors such as Ruben Amorim and Erik ten Hag.

For they too were asked about such intangibles as culture and mood and philosophy. They too were asked about more prosaic football matters such as match fitness.

It’s a conversational cycle that tells a story of recurring and systematic football failure.

Mauricio Pochettino faced reporters in his first press conference as Manchester United boss on Friday

A drone captured footage of Pochettino's first training session on Thursday

Amorim – back on a grim, foggy day exactly two years ago – was asked about Marcus Rashford and whether he had been right to spend time off in New York days before the new United manager walked through the door.

Here, Pochettino could justifiably have been asked about another forward Bryan Mbeumo spending the wee hours of Thursday morning playing the newly released Grand Theft Auto video game when he probably should have been asleep.

This is the United that Pochettino is now being asked to fix, a club where names and faces change but problems remain the same.

The Berrada interview was actually more enlightening than Pochettino’s carefully managed introduction to the wider media.

Certainly it was interesting to listen to his assertion that nine defensive players in one squad was enough. In football, as United are discovering yet again, it’s not necessarily the quantity that matters but the quality.

One point did resonate rather more deeply, though, and that was the one Berrada – once of Manchester City – made about United’s players needing a manager capable of dealing with the scrutiny of the club and who could shield some of his players from all that comes with it.

The recently-departed Michael Carrick did look rather lost on the touchline in the final tumultuous weeks of his time as manager. He didn’t look an awful lot more comfortable in front of the TV cameras either.

Bryan Mbeumo posted this picture after the midnight release of Grand Theft Auto VI

In the dressing room? Well, he lost the loyalty of his captain Bruno Fernandes towards the end and that is never a good sign.

Pochettino will do rather better at all that. The former Chelsea, PSG and Tottenham manager has a personality and a charisma that could fill an aircraft hangar. His players will arrive at Anfield for his opening game on Sunday feeling better about themselves than they have for some time.

United have hired some confidence and some authority and some experience at a time when they desperately need it, even if Berrada’s claim that they had to call the USA Federation last week to check on his release clause suggested this is an appointment made rather on the hoof.

It is, however, the impact that Pochettino can bring over time on a jumbled squad put together for six different managers over an incredible 12 years that will define him. Here, the 54-year-old undoubtedly faces challenges.

Talking this week to someone associated with Tottenham about Pochettino’s progressive seasons there between 2014 and 2019, I was reminded of the quality that the Argentinian was given to work with.

Pochettino's Spurs side harnessed the attacking power of stars including Harry Kane and Heung-min Son

The French international goalkeeper, Hugo Lloris, the Belgian central defensive partnership of Toby Alderweireld and Jan Vertonghen, England international defenders Kyle Walker, Danny Rose and Kieran Trippier and, further forward, the burgeoning attacking talents of Dele Alli, Christian Eriksen, Heung-min Son and Harry Kane.

It was a prototype Premier League football team, both in talent, age, fitness and physicality. That was why, in 2016, it almost won it.

Pochettino does not have this at Old Trafford. He doesn’t have anything like it. He has some talented players. The fact he inherits a team in the bottom three is down to Carrick’s inadequacies.

But this United squad is a mish-mash and it serves a purpose to ask how many would get in that old Spurs team we talk about.

Fernandes? Maybe. Mbeumo? Probably. That is about it and that, frankly, is where United are right now.

Pochettino has long wanted this job. It’s not a posting of convenience for him. Like others before him – men like Jose Mourinho and Louis van Gaal – he has long since coveted the cachet, the stature and the power of this remarkable football institution.

Mourinho and Van Gaal had better players than Pochettino is being handed and they both still failed, largely because they were shown to be coaches already over the top of that hill that both had worked so desperately hard to climb.

Mbeumo is one of the few United players who might have got into Pochettino's Spurs side

Where does Pochettino sit in terms of his own personal and professional growth? That is such a hard question to answer and will be utterly fundamental to how he travels in the weeks and months to come.

Sitting here fresh from the training ground and strangely seeming to question whether the glass of water in front of him was fit to drink, Pochettino declared himself to be in his coaching prime.

The proof or otherwise of that will only be revealed out on the grass. For all that he can plead valid mitigation, Pochettino was not hugely impressive in Paris or at Stamford Bridge. Before he starts to talk about dysfunctional football clubs, he may wish to take a look at his new surroundings.

Liverpool away feels like something of a free hit. Sporting in Lisbon on Wednesday less so and Brentford at home next Saturday definitely not. And so it begins. A run of 12 games in six and a half weeks that may well see Pochettino crawling into January begging for fresh legs and new players.

The new manager said here that he wishes to be across transfers and little wonder. When he looks at the mistakes made in that regard by a succession of United regimes and executives, he may indeed question what it is they put in the water in the north-west.

United fans will perhaps appreciate that one of the ‘higher ups’ at Old Trafford has finally put his head above the parapet, even if they question some of what Berrada said. That’s been overdue.

In terms of their new manager, they can be forgiven for keeping a lid on any excitement. Many of them have simply been wearied by the cycle.

#1760. Guardiola urges Portugal to ‘ensure a dignified end to Ronaldo’s career’

Syndicated reporting provided by Stats Perform and reviewed by the SoccerNews editorial team.

Pep Guardiola has called on the Portuguese Football Federation (FPF) to "ensure a dignified end to Cristiano Ronaldo's career".

Ronaldo called time on his international career earlier this month, retiring as Portugal's all-time leading scorer and appearance-maker, netting 146 goals in 234 games.

After making his debut in 2003, Ronaldo led Portugal to their first-ever major trophy at Euro 2016 and also won the Nations League in 2019 and 2025.

His time with Portugal ended abruptly, with the 41-year-old leaving their camp midway through the September-October international break after a fallout with head coach Jorge Jesus.

He was subsequently given a 30-day suspension by the FPF, though he announced his retirement ahead of the November break.

The FPF said they would plan a farewell for Ronaldo, and Guardiola has urged them to do so.

"The Portuguese Football Federation must ensure a dignified end to Cristiano Ronaldo's career," Guardiola said on Romario TV.

"Cristiano Ronaldo shouldn't leave the Portuguese national team in this manner. They can't let him go like this.

Eternamente gratos por tudo.  @Cristiano https://t.co/5g8LGQYSEz

— Portugal (@selecaoportugal) November 14, 2026

"There are exceptional players, and Cristiano Ronaldo is one of them; therefore, this situation must be rectified.

"Whether they rectify it or not isn't my concern, but they absolutely must. That's right; what he's achieved in the world of football deserves a different ending."

Messi also retired from international football this season, after Argentina finished runners-up at the 2026 World Cup.

Guardiola believes Messi and Ronaldo both helped prolong the other's career at the highest level.

"I think the two of them helped each other a great deal; if Messi hadn't had Cristiano, or if Cristiano hadn't had Messi, their careers would likely have been shorter," Guardiola added.

"But they had each other in their rearview mirrors; watching what the other was doing made them think: 'I want to be better than him, I want to win more than him'."

#1759. Sparta Prague vs. AZ Alkmaar - prediction, team news, lineups

By Seye Omidiora | 24 Nov 2026 11:47, Last updated: 24 Nov 2026 13:05

Yet to win at home in this season's Europa League, Sparta Prague welcome AZ Alkmaar to the Letna Stadium for Thursday's matchday-five encounter.

The Czech side, in turmoil after Brian Priske's recent departure, will leapfrog Leeroy Echteld's men if they secure maximum points, although doing so requires the hosts to end a three-match winless run in Europe's second-tier club competition.

Sparta remain in the qualification playoff places in 22nd, but another disappointing Europa League result this week could change that.

The Czechia side enter Thursday's matchday five encounter without a victory since the opening round, when the Maroons beat Ararat 4-1 in Armenia, having collected just one point from the next available nine.

Zelezna Sparta's four points keep them inside the playoff places on goal difference, with Celje and RB Salzburg sitting 25th and 26th respectively and six clubs, Celta, AC Milan, Jagiellonia, Viktoria Plzen, Marseille and Celtic, all on six points.

The Reds' hopes of retaining their Europa League place therefore hinge on rediscovering their form promptly as the league phase enters its second half with this week's visit from AZ.

However, their five-match winless run across all competitions, during which the Maroons have drawn two blanks and scored only once in each of their last three fixtures, appears to give their Alkmaar opponents the edge ahead of matchday five.

The abovementioned run cost Priske his job, adding to the uncertainty around the Czech giants, who ended last season second in their division but already find themselves fourth in the top flight, 13 points adrift of rivals Slavia Prague.

The visiting supporters will travel to Czechia hoping to see their side claim a third consecutive victory and return to winning ways in Europe after losing to Juventus at the halfway stage of their continental campaign.

The Cheese Farmers fell 2-1 to the Old Lady at AFAS Stadion at the start of the month, marking their third consecutive defeat and second European loss in four matches.

De Kaasboeren have since responded to those setbacks with consecutive victories over Groningen and Sparta Rotterdam, scoring nine goals in total as they beat the former 4-3 and the latter 5-1.

Mexx Meerdink starred against Groningen with two goals and an assist, while Ro-Zangelo Daal inspired the comeback victory in Rotterdam, where Echteld's in-form wide attacker scored once and set up two more.

Another away victory against the Czech giants could lift 14th-placed AZ into the coveted top eight, with seventh-placed Bayer Leverkusen three points ahead and eighth-placed Besiktas just one above the Cheese Farmers.

Sparta have several fitness concerns: Santiago Eneme and Hugo Souchurek are doubtful due to illness, while Emmanuel Uchenna (groin), Matej Rynes (ankle), Ondrej Penxa (knee) and Adam Karabec (ankle) are expected to miss out.

Tobias Guddal impressed during the home side's league defeat to Liberec, but the 24-year-old is suspended after receiving a second yellow card against Bournemouth last time out in Europe.

Having scored two of Sparta's six Europa League goals, Guddal represents a significant loss for a side whose other four strikes have come from different players.

Like the hosts, AZ have several injury concerns, with Weslley Patati, Kees Smit (groin), Lewis Schouten, Stije Resink and Jizz Hornkamp all unavailable.

While Patati has scored twice, Meerdink has contributed three of his team's seven goals, accounting for just under half of the Cheese Farmers' European tally.

Surovcik; Hoever, Kaderabek, Mbe Soh, Suchomel; Vydra, Mannsverk, Irving; Singhateh, Brunes, Alcocer

De Busser; Maikuma, Goes, Hoedt, Chavez; Koopmeiners, Kwakman, Byskov; Stengs, Meerdink, Daal

Apart from Priske's recent dismissal, Sparta's five-match winless run and Guddal's suspension leave the hosts vulnerable against an AZ side who have scored nine goals across their last two outings.

Meerdink's European scoring form and Daal's growing influence give the visitors our backing to secure a third consecutive victory and strengthen their qualification prospects.

#1758. GdS: Wins, consistency and goals for Ramos – the next steps Amorim wants Milan to take

Ruben Amorim wants to see more from his AC Milan side, starting this evening against Frosinone, and he believes they are capable.

As La Gazzetta dello Sport (seen below) report, the aim for today’s match is to ensure the break didn’t disrupt the momentum, ashat happened following the September-October pause when Milan drew away to Sassuolo.

Read SempreMilan ad-free and get access to exclusive news. Click here for a free trial!

This time, the opponent will be even tougher (at least based on league position), and Amorim knows it. For this reason, he has demanded the utmost focus from his players and has sought to fire up Gonçalo Ramos, who has only scored twice in the first 11 league matches so far.

The first issue the Portuguese forward needs to address is his finishing. In four matches – against Juventus, Lecce, Bologna, and Inter – he failed to register a single shot, while in two others (against Lazio and Genoa), he didn’t manage to hit the target.

That is simply not enough for a striker who cost €70m, plus bonuses and commissions. However, according to the former Manchester United manager, the fault does not lie with Gonçalo and instead is a team issue.

“Having another forward to assist Ramos and Camarda would certainly be an extra option, but our real problem is that we aren’t reaching the final 30 metres. We are among the worst teams in Serie A when it comes to shots taken and chances created,” he said in his press conference.

“As for Gonçalo, we aren’t putting him in a position to score. Cissé gets into the box with his runs, while Ramos relies on the team’s build-up play. In Genoa, both of our goals came thanks to him. We need to support him better through more possession and quick passing combinations in the final third.

“My goal is to win matches while helping the players perform at their best. We signed Ramos to score goals, but right now, he is helping me more than I am helping him.” A candid admission in defence of the striker he personally pushed to sign.

Compared to the win in Genoa two Sundays ago, Amorim is leaning toward not fielding four attacking players (Moreira, Cisse, Pulisic, and Ramos) from the start.

In yesterday’s training sessions, Cisse was left out of the starting line-up, which featured Musah and Modric in the middle, with Rabiot pushed further forward behind Gonçalo. Pavlovic has been called up and is eager to start, though he is not yet at 100% fitness.

“The choice of formation depends on the opponent and the team’s current state. I don’t believe that scoring more goals or winning more matches is necessarily linked to fielding more attacking players. Frosinone is an attractive side to watch, and speed is their primary weapon,” Amorim added.

“We rank second in Serie A for the number of sprints, and we have the tools to counter both their pace and their one-on-one ability on the flanks. We’ll need to be focused, as they commit more players to the final third than we do and are more clinical than us when winning the ball back.

“As for our season so far? I’m not satisfied with fourth place or all of our performances. We need to play better and achieve more in Europe, but we have grown as a team and in our overall attitude. We must keep moving in this direction.”

He concluded by sharing a Christmas wish regarding the transfer market: “January signings shouldn’t be based on the current league table, but rather on long-term planning. My Christmas wish is for us to win our next seven matches and get our injured players back. That is what I’d like.”

#1757. Iraola fumes at bungling fourth official for costing Liverpool a penalty

Andoni Iraola wanted to talk about his team and their need to improve but how could he concentrate on something so straightforward when he had seen something so bizarre?

It is important, first and foremost, to explain this is not painting a narrative about Liverpool being unfortunate. Far from it. Iraola hissed his dismay that Nottingham Forest had shown more intensity and been the better team for long periods in an entertaining 2-2 draw.

But the penalty that changed the contest? Iraola, his coaching staff, even the supporters behind the dugout had been left flabbergasted that the malfunctioning number board of fourth official Tim Robinson presented an avenue for Forest to exploit.

Iraola had tried to make a triple change, wanting to introduce Ryan Gravenberch, Kostas Tsimikas and Rio Ngumoha, but as Robinson pressed buttons to no avail and everyone in Red became frustrated, Forest substitute Liam Delap took a quick throw and the Liverpool house almost caved in.

Neco Williams, once of Liverpool, surged into the penalty area, Alisson Becker arrived a fraction too late after the defender got his shot away and took his old team-mate down. Morgan Gibbs-White exacerbated the damage when sending Alisson the wrong way and this was the last thing a manager wanting to make an impression on a big day needed to see but this was reality.

Alisson takes out Neco Williams and Forest have a penalty! 😱📺 Watch live on TNT Sports & HBO Max pic.twitter.com/fX2flY3Tob

Gibbs-White converts from the spot to restore Forest's lead! 🌳🎯📺 Watch live on TNT Sports & HBO Max pic.twitter.com/jeoPiXPArw

“I cannot explain because I don’t have an explanation,” Iraola said. “I wanted to make those substitutions about three minutes before. I mean, it was two, three, four times the ball had gone out. I still don’t know the reason why we couldn’t make the subs.

“I think [the fourth official] was having some problems with the board or something. It [the penalty] wouldn’t have happened if I had made the sub. I asked. I had complained the previous time. The supporters were shouting and they were aware of the situation. But I don’t know what happened and I don’t know why they have given the penalty.”

"A professional fourth official cannot take three minutes." 😳Andoni Iraola was not happy with the time taken to get the substitutes' board ready.🎙️ @jules_breach | 📺 TNT Sports & HBO Max pic.twitter.com/fMfYOjQJPd

He did know, though, why Liverpool had needed to drag themselves off the deck again for the second week in a row. Iraola has shown in his opening weeks on Merseyside that he is not someone who seeks excuses.

“A lack of intensity hurt us,” Iraola said with obvious disdain and it was only down to a show of character in the second period that a slovenly first half did not enable Forest to win at Anfield for the third consecutive year, for all that the travelling fans thought it was “happening again!”

Forest, bruised after two defeats in four days to Leeds, looked like an Oliver Glasner side. They were aggressive and well organised, the only failing was that physically they could not see the job through, but the Austrian insisted that will change in due course.

Once Glasner is settled in and he gets his transfer business done – “definitely one, possibly two and probably three,” was his mischievous reply to how the window will unfold – Forest will be a formidable proposition, especially if the first 45 minutes are a barometer.

They had been knocking on the door before Dan Ndoye eventually broke the deadlock, sweeping a left-footed drive past Alisson after Igor Jesus had won a header from a long clearance. It was a simple goal, marginally onside, but it was absolutely deserved.

Ndoye gives Forest the lead at Anfield! 🌳🔥📺 Watch live on TNT Sports & HBO Max pic.twitter.com/ag0oZ7UjTm

“There were many positive aspects,” said Glasner. “It has been a three-game week; some players played. We are getting more and more fitness, that is just the foundation of how we want to play. It is just a point but it still feels a bit frustrating, so we have to stay humble.”

"I think we were very poor in the first half." 😤Andoni Iraola gives his assessment of Liverpool's performance against Nottingham Forest.🎙️ @jules_breach | 📺 TNT Sports & HBO Max pic.twitter.com/COZfhwkLeX

Neco Williams and James McAtee react to Nottingham Forest's draw at Anfield 🌳🎙️ @lynseyhipgrave1 | 📺 TNT Sports & HBO Max pic.twitter.com/BjX0p1yQ1m

"We started the game pretty bad today." 😬Alexander Isak gives his assessment of Liverpool's performance at Anfield.🎙️ @jules_breach | 📺 TNT Sports & HBO Max pic.twitter.com/3wD0hplmQ6

The playmaker added another goal and assist to his tally this afternoon.

20 - Morgan Gibbs-White has been directly involved in 20 goals in 2026 (15 goals, 5 assists), the joint-most of any Premier League player in all competitions (level with Haaland).His 13 goals in the Premier League in 2026 are also the most of any player.Decisive. pic.twitter.com/p1wQFwXvsI

Liverpool and Forest are both made to wait for their first Premier League wins of the season as the two sides play out a pulsating 2-2 draw at Anfield.

Full-time scenes at Anfield as Liverpool and Nottingham Forest share the points 🤝📺 Watch live on TNT Sports & HBO Max pic.twitter.com/WqOpfU38es

Sels calmly comes out to claim a deep cross to relieve the pressure on Forest. Munoz runs back to dispossess Delap and win a free kick, giving Liverpool another chance to launch the ball forward.

Glasner makes a very late double change as Hudson-Odoi and Dominguez replace McAtee and Igor Jesus.

There will be five minutes of added time. Liverpool continue their relentless search for a third goal, while Forest are holding on.

It’s wave after wave of Liverpool pressure. Forest are camped inside their own half. Igor Jesus and Delap are chasing every loose ball, but Forest are struggling to get out at the moment.

Munoz’s goal has provided another twist in this pulsating encounter. Isak wins a free kick in such dangerous territory and Szoboszlai steps up to take it. The Hungarian slams a venomous effort wide of the far post. Can either side find a late winner?

What an incredible finish! Wirtz threads a delightful pass through to Munoz. With his back to goal, the winger swivels and takes the ball on the outside of Murillo, before smashing a thunderous effort into the roof of the net, which brushes the crossbar on its way in.

Munoz, take a bow! 🤯👏📺 Watch live on TNT Sports & HBO Max pic.twitter.com/GD8IAdy2rJ

Igor Jesus does brilliantly to escape Nyoni, before he is pulled to the ground by Arajou, who is booked. It’s been an excellent defensive effort from Forest.

Iraola makes his final two alterations as Araujo and Nyoni replace Jacquet and Mac Allister.  Szoboszlai then swings such an inviting delivery into the penalty area, but Isak miscues his strike with his left foot.

Amid the chaos, Alisson was booked just before the penalty after appealing the decision and Iraola has ordered a triple change, taking off Kerkez, Frimpong and Gakpo for Tsimikas, Gravenberch and Ngumoha. This has seen Szoboszlai move out to right back.

Andoni Iraola is about to make his substitution and this is interesting because he had planned to introduce Rio Ngumoha, Kostas Tsimikas and Ryan Gravenberch 10 minutes ago but told them to sit down after Liverpool had equalised. Forest have put Liam Delap on, giving him his debut after completing his £45m move to the club.

The Forest captain sends Alisson the wrong way, powering a clinical penalty into the net. Gibbs-White demonstrates fantastic composure and Liverpool have it all to do again.

Gibbs-White converts from the spot to restore Forest's lead! 🌳🎯📺 Watch live on TNT Sports & HBO Max pic.twitter.com/jeoPiXPArw

Delap showcases excellent initiative and takes a quick throw-in to send Williams through on goal. Alisson rushes out and catches Williams as he attempts to lob the goalkeeper. Williams crashes to the ground and the referee points to the spot. Alisson is furious. What a chance for Forest to restore their lead.

Alisson takes out Neco Williams and Forest have a penalty! 😱📺 Watch live on TNT Sports & HBO Max pic.twitter.com/fX2flY3Tob

This game is being played at a ferocious pace and Forest’s club-record signing Delap enters the action as he replaces Ndoye. Can the former Chelsea striker mark his debut with a much-needed goal?

That leveller has injected so much energy into Liverpool. Anfield believes again. Isak really needed that goal.

So much credit must go to Gakpo. The winger shrugs off Williams and fires a pinpoint cross towards the back post. Isak is there and converts from close range. We’re set up for such an intriguing finale. Liverpool have the momentum now.

Isak equalises for Liverpool at the Kop end! 🔴🔥📺 Watch live on TNT Sports & HBO Max pic.twitter.com/qKFxq2AqaB

Wirtz’s frustrating afternoon is compounded as he picks up a booking after hauling Murillo to the ground. Iraola looks to be readying some substitutions.

There is a very strange feeling here: it’s almost a case of the home fans waiting for Nottingham Forest to score a second goal rather than anticipating that Liverpool will equalise. The early buzz in the atmosphere has gone and that is because the gaps everyone can see in the make up of the team remain. How Bradley Barcola will transform this situation?

Jacquet’s pass is intercepted and Ndoye is released on the counter. He’s guided out wide by Van Dijk but still squeezes in a brilliant cross. Gibbs-White was running up the pitch in support and slowed down, meaning no one was there to turn in Ndoye’s delivery.

Munoz is the next player to be booked after reacting angrily to a decision. Iraola has to consider making some changes soon.

Aina catches Munoz with a late challenge and he’s the second Forest player to go into the referee’s book.

You can already see in this second half that there is acres of space for Forest to exploit on the counter as Liverpool push for a leveller. Munoz then heads a point-blank header over the bar. Luckily for the Spaniard, the offside flag was up against Gakpo.

We are back for the second half here at Anfield. Can Liverpool find a route back into this game or can Forest hold onto the three points?

It’s a bizarre situation for Liverpool. They could easily be level or be 2-0 down. But they trial just 1-0 at half-time. Wirtz and Gakpo are looking lively, but Isak has struggled to influence the game.

Dan Ndoye scores his first goal in the Premier League in 377 days 🤯 pic.twitter.com/tjSiGoSPyW

Forest have a slender one-goal advantage at the break after a frantic first half at Anfield. Ndoye curled the visitors into a well-deserved lead after 24 minutes, before Wirtz had a goal ruled out for offside. The German was then sensationally denied by Sels’ diving save as he tipped Wirtz’s header over the bar. Alisson then replicated Sels’ heroics, parrying Igor Jesus’ strike against the woodwork to stop Forest from doubling their lead.

What a move and what a save! Murillo sprays an inch-perfect pass out to Aina, who chops inside of Munoz and fires a low cross into Igor Jesus. The Forest striker shoots first-time from inside the penalty area, but his effort is sensationally parried onto the bar by Alisson. That is a world-class stop from the Brazilian goalkeeper.

A world-class save from Alisson denies Forest a second! 🤯🧤📺 Watch live on TNT Sports & HBO Max pic.twitter.com/4NtzROILrU

Igor Jesus receives the game’s first yellow card after clipping Mac Allister with an unnecessary challenge.

Liverpool then fly forward again as Gakpo nutmegs Williams. His cross trickles through to Munoz at the back post. The ball is slightly behind Munoz and he leans back before shooting, causing his strike to narrowly sail over the bar.

There will be three minutes of added time to conclude this first half.

Liverpool are applying all the pressure at the end of this first half. At times, Forest have had every outfield player behind the ball.

Sels makes a superb save! Gakpo takes on his marker on the outside and fires in a cross which Wirtz meets. The attacker gets in between Schlager and Aina to win the header, but his effort is excellently tipped over the bar by Sels.

Out of nothing, Liverpool are level. McAtee attempts to play out from a deep position and his pass is intercepted by Wirtz. The ball breaks to Frimpong, who slips a clever pass to Wirtz. The German playmaker swivels and slides a low effort into the bottom corner. It’s a brilliant finish, but Frimpong was in an offside position before he provided the assist. VAR confirms this and Liverpool’s joy has been cut short. That is a huge let off for Forest, who need to be more careful with possession in deeper areas.

Following that Forest goal, there was a small flurry of Liverpool pressure, with Szoboszlai having a free kick punched away by Sels. Murillo is then very careless with the ball and is dispossessed. This allowed Mac Allister to play in Isak, but the striker is crowded out by multiple Forest defenders before he can get a shot away.

For the third season in a row, Nottingham Forest lead at Anfield. The goal had been coming, too. Liverpool were bright early but suddenly big gaps have started appearing and Forest are wily enough to exploit. There are lots of gripes around the stands about it being “too easy” and this knowledgeable crowd are right. A long ball forward and a simple flick has caused mayhem.

Forest are ahead and are well worth their lead. Sels launches a long ball up to Igor Jesus, who takes it down with an exquisite touch. The ball then breaks to Gibbs-White. The Forest captain plays in Ndoye and the winger curls a clinical effort into the far bottom corner to send the away support wild.

Ndoye gives Forest the lead at Anfield! 🌳🔥📺 Watch live on TNT Sports & HBO Max pic.twitter.com/ag0oZ7UjTm

Liverpool are struggling to find any space in and around Forest’s midfield and defence. Isak and Wirtz have been on the periphery as the time ticks over midway point of the first half.

Huge chance for Forest! McAtee drops deep and picks out Ndoye with a teasing cross. The forward meets the delivery and his header bounces wide. Upon the replays, there looks to have been a push on Frimpong by Ndoye. The referee’s whistle wasn’t sounded so it would have been interesting to see what would of happened if that chance had been converted.

It’s been a really frantic start to this game. Out of possession, Forest are retreating into a really rigid back five formation. Going forward, Aina and Williams are getting up the pitch at every opportunity.

Aina stands up an inviting cross to the back post for Ndoye, who heads it back into the danger zone. Igor Jesus latches onto it, but Jacquet makes a goal-saving tackle to block the striker’s close-range effort.

Sensational block from Jeremy Jacquet to deny Igor Jesus! 🤯📺 Watch live on TNT Sports & HBO Max pic.twitter.com/XuhO1GuE9F

Van Dijk clips a long ball over to the onrushing Isak as Liverpool look to burst forward on the counter. Isak races onto it and enters the penalty area, but he’s chased by Jair Cunha who matches the striker for pace. There’s a shoulder-to-shoulder, and the Forest defender bumps Isak off the ball, before Milenkovic comes back to mop up the danger.

Ndoye attempts to sprint in behind Liverpool’s defence. He’s chased by Jacquet and Ndoye can’t quite take the ball under his spell. That is an early warning sign for Liverpool.

The hosts then go up the other end as Mac Allister threads a delightful pass through to Gakpo. The Liverpool forward tries to swivel and shoot, but Williams tracks back and makes a crucial tackle.

Frimpong gets in behind Forest’s backline and attempts to pick out Gakpo with a cross aimed towards the back post. However, the ball bobbles and the Liverpool right back overhits his delivery.

A very intriguing team selected by Andoni Iraola and one that illustrates his confidence. It could be viewed as big call to drop Ryan Gravenberch and Rio Ngumoha but Victor Munoz and Alexis Mac Allister both made a difference when they were introduced at St James’s Park last Sunday and they warrant their inclusion. Munoz won’t be fit enough to play 90 minutes but it will be fascinating to watch him, particularly as Bradley Barcola will soon arrive to play in the same position on the left flank.

We are now under way at Anfield. Can Iraola mark his first competitive home game with a win or will Glasner get up and running with Forest?

A roaring rendition of You’ll Never Walk Alone has just boomed around Anfield. We will now observe a minute’s applause for Liverpool legend Kevin Keegan, who passed away at the age of 75 in July.

Anfield remembers Kevin Keegan ❤️A special tribute to the Liverpool legend ahead of kick-off. pic.twitter.com/bJgi58vPj7

A very poignant and colourful tribute to Kevin Keegan, with Anfield paying its respects to one of its favourite sons. The atmosphere is good and the onus is on the team to maintain it. This won’t be easy, as Nottingham Forest arrive here with a point to prove under Oliver Glasner. The big story with Forest will come later, with their pursuit of Everton’s Harrison Armstrong. It it is a transfer that is causing huge discussion on Merseyside.

Both sets of players are out onto the pitch and are met by an electric atmosphere at Anfield.

All set for #LIVNFO 💪 pic.twitter.com/IJOZ6NwGNW

Earlier this month, Liverpool owners Fenway Sports Group announced they had agreed to sell a minority equity stake to 1892 Holdings, a consortium led and managed by Amit Bhatia, who is in attendance at Anfield today.

On the development, Bhatia told Liverpool’s website: “It feels incredible. It feels surreal when I hear those words, obviously an incredibly proud moment for myself, for my family, for our partners. We’re talking about Liverpool Football Club here, right? I mean, we’re talking about the greatest football club in the world. And so to have the ability to be involved in any capacity is a huge privilege and a huge honour.”

Having been linked to both Tottenham Hotspur and Manchester City, Cody Gakpo’s Liverpool future has looked doubtful at points this summer.

However, Spurs’ signings of Savinho and Omar Marmoush, as well as Manchester City’s potentially big-money pursuit of Enzo Fernandez, means that any exit for the Dutchman looks extremely complicated.

Gakpo scored Liverpool’s first equaliser in their chaotic 2-2 draw with Newcastle United and starts today on the left wing.

❤️ https://t.co/MgbTcQWank pic.twitter.com/DwIooN2OFk

In September 2024, Nottingham Forest claimed their first win over Liverpool at Anfield in 55 years thanks to Callum Hudson-Odoi’s sumptuous 72nd-minute curler.

When Callum Hudson-Odoi made history at Anfield 🤩 pic.twitter.com/HhJ73WztMd

Last season’s emphatic 3-0 victory in the same fixture under Sean Dyche means that Forest have successive wins at a ground where they could notoriously never manage three points.

Nottingham Forest have smashed their club-record transfer fee to sign Chelsea striker Liam Delap for £50m on a five-year deal, ending a lengthy pursuit by both the club and their head coach Oliver Glasner.

Last summer Delap held talks with Forest and Glasner, while he was in charge at Crystal Palace, before he opted to join his mentor and former Manchester City Under-21 coach Enzo Maresca at Stamford Bridge.

One of the summer’s most talked about and protracted transfer pursuits is nearing its conclusion as Liverpool have agreed a £120m deal with Paris St-Germain to sign Bradley Barcola.

The Frenchman was absent from PSG’s squad on Friday evening as Luis Enrique’s side drew 2-2 with Lille in Ligue 1.

Barcola is yet another big-money addition to Liverpool’s forward line, following on from the signings of Alexander Isak, Florian Wirtz and Hugo Ekitike last summer.

He also has the approval of club legend Steven Gerrard, who is at Anfield on duty for TNT Sports.

"Incredible talent." 🌟Steven Gerrard reacts to Liverpool's pursuit of Bradley Barcola.🎙️ @OliviaBuzaglo | 📺 Watch live on TNT Sports & HBO Max pic.twitter.com/bVd7odopa3

"It was the shared vision." 🤝Oliver Glasner on why he chose to join the Nottingham Forest project 👀 pic.twitter.com/ldxjwU8FW4

"For me, it's a special game, definitely." ❤️Andoni Iraola looks ahead to his first Premier League game at Anfield as Liverpool boss.🎙️ @jules_breach | 📺 Watch live on TNT Sports & HBO Max pic.twitter.com/fukilMigKz

Liverpool: Alisson, Frimpong, Jacquet, van Dijk, Kerkez, Szoboszlai, Mac Allister, Munoz, Wirtz, Gakpo, Isak.

Subs: Mamardashvili, Endo, Tsimikas, Araujo, Gravenberch, Nyoni, McConnell, Koumas, Ngumoha.

Nottingham Forest: Sels, Jair Cunha, Milenkovic, Murillo, Aina, Schlager, McAtee, Williams, Ndoye, Gibbs-White, Igor Jesus.

Subs: John Victor, Diomande, Hudson-Odoi, Dominguez, Wood, Delap, Yates, Netz, Abbott.

It's good to be back 😍 @Expedia pic.twitter.com/IGv6d9Pbhq

Having only joined up with his teammates a couple of days ago, new signing Liam Delap begins his Nottingham Forest career on the bench, with Igor Jesus preferred as the central striker.

Lining up at Liverpool. 📋 pic.twitter.com/1gtQ7BQz5J

Andoni Iraola has made two changes to the side that drew with Newcastle United. Victor Munoz starts with Rio Ngumoha on the bench. The other alteration sees Alexis Mac Allister replace Ryan Gravenberch in midfield.

Team news is IN! 🔴 #LIVNFO pic.twitter.com/3avoOQOPrM

Anfield will host its first Premier League match of the 2026-27 season.

Good morning and welcome to our live coverage of this Premier League match between Liverpool and Nottingham Forest at Anfield.

This encounter pits two summer appointments – Andoni Iraola and Oliver Glasner – against each other as they both search for their first top-flight win at their new clubs.

In the opening Premier League game-week, Iraola’s Liverpool needed a last-gasp 99th-minute penalty from Dominik Szoboszlai to rescue an unconvincing 2-2 draw with Newcastle United at St. James’ Park. Meanwhile, Nottingham Forest have suffered back-to-back home defeats in four days against Leeds United without scoring (1-0 Premier League, 2-0 Carabao Cup).

Iraola has been handed the unenviable task of steering Liverpool back on track following a hugely disappointing campaign under Arne Slot, whose side’s defence of their Premier League ended in a meek fifth-place finish despite spending more than £400m in the previous summer.

The former Bournemouth boss must uncover how to get the best out of big-money recruits such as Alexander Isak, Florian Wirtz, Milos Kerkez and Jeremie Frimpong, and also tighten up Liverpool’s vulnerable midfield and defence. Given the pressure of the job and the club’s hectic schedule while balancing domestic and European football, it’s a tough ask. However, Liverpool have agreed a £120m deal for Paris St-Germain winger Bradley Barcola to bolster their attacking reinforcements, but the transfer hasn’t been finalised in time for today’s match.

Last season, Forest endured an equally tumultuous campaign, churning through a staggering four managers, before eventually stumbling to a 16th-place finish. Glasner has been hand-picked by owner Evangelos Marinakis to usher in an era of stability and success, after winning the FA Cup, Community Shield and Conference League in just over two years at Crystal Palace.

Both Marinakis and Glasner are extremely ambitious and demanding figures. You’d imagine a top-half finish would be considered the absolute minimum for Forest, while Glasner’s track record of winning trophies surely indicates that Marinakis is eyeing some silverware at the City Ground.

It’s a meeting of two managers who must deliver. Three points for either side would serve as a much-needed tonic to kickstart their seasons.

Kick-off is at 12:30, with team news coming shortly.

Barcelona will continue their Champions League league stage campaign with a contest against Azerbaijani outfit Sabah on Wednesday evening.

The Owls had never played in the European Cup before this season, and they will now be taking on one of the biggest club teams in European football.

Thomas Frank revealed Ismaila Sarr's injury is still "touch and go" and ruled the winger out for Crystal Palace's Europa League encounter with Real Sociedad.

Sarr has missed each of Palace's last six games with a groin injury, last appearing in their 2-2 draw with Besiktas on October 22.

The 28-year-old scored 21 goals across 45 games in all competitions last season, marking the best scoring campaign of his career.

Since his move to Selhurst in August 2024, Sarr (41 – 33 goals, eight assists) has directly contributed to the joint-most goals among Palace players, along with Jean-Philippe Mateta.

However, Sarr will have to wait longer to appear under Frank, who took over from Pierre Sage during the international break.

"Sarr, that will not be a long, long one, but it will be weeks before he can help the team," said Frank.

#1753. Liverpool transfer news: Reds 'ready to battle' for £37.7m attacker familiar to Jurgen Klopp

By Oliver Thomas | 24 Nov 2026 12:22

Liverpool are reportedly among a number of clubs interested in signing Borussia Monchengladbach wonderkid Wael Mohya.

Earlier this month, the 17-year-old attacker earned his first-ever senior international call-up to Jurgen Klopp’s Germany squad after making a notable impression as a first-team regular at club level.

Mohya broke into Monchengladbach’s senior side midway through last season and became the club’s youngest-ever goalscorer against Bayern Munich in March of this year.

He has since developed into an increasingly influential player under head coach Alexander Blessin this term, featuring in all 10 Bundesliga matches as well as two DFB-Pokal games.

Mohya became the fourth youngest-player in Bundesliga history to score in consecutive games in October, contributing with a goal and an assist in a standout display in a 3-2 win against Stuttgart.

The dynamic and versatile attacker, who is comfortable operating centrally or out wide, has produced several impressive performances that have subsequently caught the eye of some of Europe’s biggest clubs.

According to TEAMtalk, Andoni Iraola’s Liverpool have shown concrete interest in Mohya and have intensively scouted the teenager.

The report adds the Reds are ‘ready to battle’ with high-flying Brighton & Hove Albion, who currently sit second in the Premier League table and have also been closely monitoring the attacker.

Bundesliga giants Bayern Munich, Borussia Dortmund, Bayer Leverkusen and RB Leipzig are also said to be keeping an eye on Mohya’s progress, while Real Madrid, Barcelona and AC Milan are some of the big clubs abroad who have recently entered the race for his signature.

As things stand, Monchengladbach are yet to receive any formal offers for Mohya or enter negotiations with another club despite growing interest in his services.

Mohya’s contract is due to expire in June 2028, and Monchengladbach sporting director Rouven Schroder recently insisted that “he is definitely not for sale in January,” adding: “The rest will depend on how the market develops.”

The youngster is viewed as a key part of Monchengladbach’s plans for this season, and it is understood that an offer in the region of €45m (£37.7m) is what it would take to persuade the German club to open talks over a possible sale in the coming transfer windows.
